sentences.text: The type species of this genus is Fluvioviridavis platyrhamphus.
It stands alone as the only genus within its own family, Fluvioviridavidae.
The genus was formally described by Mayr in 2005.
However, the name was originally coined by Mayr and Daniels in 2001.
Two additional species, F. michaeldanielsi and F. nazensis, were later named by Mayr and Kitchener in 2024.
Currently, the Paleobiology Database records five fossil occurrences of this creature.
Remains have been discovered in the Early Eocene Green River Formation of Wyoming and the London Clay Formation of the United Kingdom.
This animal lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
